title: Around 3.5 million Brits hit switch amidst cost-of-living concerns
discussion_signal: The post interprets Ofcom switching figures through cost-of-living pressure, out-of-contract inertia, missed bills, downgrades, and cancellations, showing how exit friction and affordability shape whether competition produces usable consumer power.
linked_research_question: When telecom switching becomes an affordability response, how can exit friction convert competition into consumer harm or prevent effective remedy?
limits: The post is secondary commentary and does not provide the Ofcom dataset
Switching counts do not show whether consumers obtained better outcomes
Commercial interpretation may emphasize market opportunity alongside consumer risk
